target.description: 4 iterated AES rounds on 128-bit blocks in the source's independent-round-key model. setting.key_relation: One complete cipher key is a tuple of independently uniformly sampled 128-bit round keys, including the independent input key mask. It is not derived by the AES-128, AES-192 or AES-256 master-key schedule.
setting.key_population: Uniform independent-round-key ensemble for the AES 128-bit round structure; bounds average over the tuple of round keys, not over standard AES master keys.
setting.plaintext_model: For differential statements, any prescribed nonzero input/output difference and the source DDT averaging over input u; the independent input key mask makes averaging over the keys alone equivalent. For pairwise independence, any pair of distinct fixed plaintexts.
assumptions: The categorical single_secret_key denotes one sampled whole round-key tuple, not a standard 128/192/256-bit AES master key; independence is part of the explicit population definition.

Expected differential probability is averaged over the independent round-key ensemble. The paper does not prove the same bounds for every fixed round-key tuple, almost all fixed tuples, or the standard AES key schedule.
The source uses the concrete AES Sbox, ShiftRows and MixColumns, with b=128, k=4 and w=8; generic AES-like auxiliary lemmas are not being promoted to an AES result without its concrete constants.

property.scope: Concrete four-round 128-bit AES round transformation and its inverse under independent round keys. Collision probability concerns the entire output-difference distribution, not a single characteristic or maximum differential probability.

success.description: Exact equal-prior classification success of the explicit one-pair test: query P and P XOR DeltaX0 and output AES iff GammaX2 dot (C XOR Cprime)=0. Table5/Figure9a diagonal differences reach only column0 after the first full round; the binary SR/MC-adjoint of GammaX2 is supported at row-major indices1,6,11, disjoint from that column. Thus AES acceptance is1 for every fixed key and plaintext, without independent-round or averaged-key assumptions. Under a uniform128-bit permutation, the nonzero output difference is uniform: exactly2^127-1 of2^128-1 differences have zero parity. The displayed success is slightly above75%, not100%; advantage is2^127/(2^128-1). The primary value remains an exact symbolic rational, not the source correlation1 or a measured rate. Its two chosen-plaintext blocks are a derived count for this specified test; no previously fixed source budget is changed. Three- to five-round endpoints are not covered by this deterministic argument.

success.description: Conditional eventual completion of the native Section4.2 construction. Fix admissible outer choices \(C\), including the nonzero active differences. Before any return, define \(G_j(C)\subseteq\{0,1\}^{32}\) as the diagonal values whose computed \(\Delta x_4\) column belongs to its four native compatibility lists, for \(j=0,1,2,3\). The feasibility condition is \(\mathcal F(C): |G_j(C)|>0\) for every column. The operational policy \(\mathcal S\) interprets each native choice as fresh iid uniform32-bit sampling; the source says choose a value and does not print an iid theorem. With \(q_j=|G_j(C)|/2^{32}\), the native loop has \(\Pr[T_j>t\mid C]=(1-q_j)^t\) and \(E[T_j\mid C]=1/q_j\). Feasibility gives almost-sure termination of all four loops without independence between columns. Figure12 then deterministically completes a valid standard AES256 key, and outward propagation yields \(W\): the full distinct-message, same-chosen-key Property1 witness in the prescribed input/output subspaces. Here \(\tau\) is total native stopping time. The probability of feasibility over outer choices remains unquantified. The source mean16 trials and approximately2^8 basic-operation cost separately assume \(q_j\approx2^{-4}\); nonemptiness alone does not establish that estimate. This model is not unconditional AES success, success within a fixed2^8-work cap, or distinguishing advantage.

assumptions: Arithmetic is over GF(2^8) in the AES polynomial basis, with a/0=0, including at a=0.

target.description: 4-round AES-128 in Table 1's secret-key scope; X0 plaintext, X1 after whitening, X5 final output without MixColumns (Section 2.2). Source probability approximations are not every-standard-master-key theorems.

setting.key_relation: One fixed unknown AES-128 master key supplies all queries; no related-key access.

setting.plaintext_model: Independent delta-sets varying one chosen plaintext byte over all256 values, others constant.
setting.reference_model: Source concrete-AES-DDT joint two-zero-byte probability, compared with the corresponding uniform-permutation event; not a completed distinguishing cost vector.
assumptions: Section 2.3 assumes no nontrivial relation between delta-sets and uses a normal statistical approximation.
Introduction explicitly invokes independent random round keys for extended probabilities; no every-master-key proof under the standard AES key schedule is supplied.

property.statement: Table3 i0=15, source first-column indices(2,3) reports joint probability p≈2^-16-2^-29.955. These are intermediate DeltaX4 bytes before the final SB/SR, transported to final DeltaX5 zero bytes(10,7) with final MC omitted. This joint probability is distinct from the conditional statistic used for the attack.
property.quantifier: Author probability model averaged over relevant differences, with explicit round-key/column assumptions; not a theorem for every standard fixed master key.
property.scope: 4-round AES-128 in Table 1's secret-key scope; X0 plaintext, X1 after whitening, X5 final output without MixColumns (Section 2.2). Source probability approximations are not every-standard-master-key theorems.

success.description: Derived distinguishing-advantage lower bound for the exact Section3.2 endpoint. The CC/no-AK5 test decrypts its fixed rank32 equality subspace of2^96 ciphertexts and tests plaintext-byte balance. Ideal acceptance implies that the fixed plaintext byte at row0,column0 equals0 exactly2^88 times. In a uniform128-bit permutation, or its inverse, the relevant2^96-image subset is sampled without replacement. With Q=2^128, K=2^120, M=2^96 and k=2^88, the single-count probability is exactly h=binom(K,k)*binom(Q-K,M-k)/binom(Q,M). Mean-atom Stirling inequalities yield h<2^-44; the proof is retained in the B40 report. The complete conjunction has false-positive probability below2^-44. AES acceptance is one by the stored balance property, giving the displayed advantage bound. No independence between four counts or cosets, source-normal approximation, or disputed2^-40.7 scalar is used. AppendixD.2 models every non-centred convolution coefficient as Bin(2^31,1/2). With separation s=31, a coefficient exceeds the safe lane range only when all2^31 indicators equal1, model probability2^(-2^31). For two packed lanes at n=32, the largest requested parity position31 is below64-n=32, so modular FFT overflow cannot reach it when lower-lane coefficients are safe. Bounding all coefficients, not just the right-key lane, across six sets, eight output bits,2^8 outer bytes and2^32 convolution outputs gives packing-failure envelope epsilon<=48*2^(40-2^31). Together with the ideal wrong-output envelope2^-8, the union bound gives P_model>=255/256-epsilon without any independence between coefficients or between packing and wrong-output events. PDF21 Section4.3 gives PS>0.99 for one correct8-bit relation ranked first at D=T=2^90 and repeats the procedure16times at the existing D=T=2^94. Let E_i be correctness of repetition i. The marginal rates inherit the source quartet/counter independence and normal/order-statistic approximations of Section3.2. success.description: Equal-prior classification success under the MRSA23 printed-loop model at the original RBH17 nominal assignment $t=1$, $x=2^{30}$, $y=2^{93}$. Define $u=2^{-32}$, $h=2y$, $c_m(u)=\binom{4}{m}u^m(1-u)^{4-m}$ and $H(a,b;u)=\sum_{r=a}^{b}c_r(u)$, with empty sums zero. Let $s=\sum_{m=0}^{t-1}c_m(u)(1-H(4-t,3-m;u))^h+\sum_{m=t}^{3}c_m(u)$ and $z=(1-H(4-t,3;u))^h$. The two terms are AES acceptance and correct random-permutation rejection, not distinguishing advantage. Model arithmetic rounds the balanced result to approximately0.5; no exact0.5 scalar is stored. Original native $D=2xy=2^{124}$ is unchanged; the corresponding individual-query nominal cap is $4xy=2^{125}$, not actual or mean stopping cost. This is an Atlas symbolic specialization of the published MRSA23 author model, not a printed t1/t3 scalar, experiment, exact adaptive-permutation theorem or verified effective attack. It describes the literal capped Algorithms5/3 test schedule, without an extra terminal discard: current plaintext and ciphertext pairs are checked, but the final decrypted pair is not checked again. RBH17 separately describes discarding one-active-word swap inputs; equivalence to a program applying that rule immediately at the terminal swap is unresolved. Source conditional-binomial and within-/between-chain independence assumptions, distinct-pair normalization and terminal-policy applicability remain pending.

success.description: Author estimate approximately63% complete secret-key recovery, explicitly1-1/e in full-version Section9.3, for the tracked-quartet/high-memory eight-round AES128 endpoint. The source does not guarantee distinct adaptively produced quartets; this is its coverage model, not a rigorous probability bound or an empirical success fraction. target.description: Supporting identities for each byte inverse used in full AES-128 encryption and its actual key schedule, written in the conjugate BES coordinates. These identities are mathematical components, not a completed attack or an unconditional replacement for the reported no-zero MQ system.

setting.key_relation: One ordinary AES128 master key; embedded schedule must retain conjugacy and the actual AES key-schedule constraints.
setting.key_population: general secret key
setting.plaintext_model: AES16-byte plaintext/key and their conjugate embeddings; never arbitrary unrelated BES state/key vectors.
assumptions: For a byte w in GF(2^8), x is the canonical AES inverse x=w^254, including0 mapped to0.
The coordinates x_m=x^(2^m), w_m=w^(2^m) obey conjugacy; m is modulo8.
The two identities are necessary but not sufficient by themselves: x=0,w=1 also satisfies them, so no unique inverse encoding or solved system follows.

time.note: Supporting algebraic identity, not a cryptanalytic resource measurement.

data.note: Supporting algebraic identity, not a cryptanalytic resource measurement.

memory.note: Supporting algebraic identity, not a cryptanalytic resource measurement.

preprocessing.note: Supporting algebraic identity, not a cryptanalytic resource measurement.

success.description: Exact component identities, not online attack success or solver performance.

evidence.locator: PDF p.14 / printed p.14, Section6.2 paragraph beginning the additional simple quadratic equations.
evidence.interpretation: Supporting exact necessary identities, kept distinct from a complete representation or claimed attack cost.

property.statement: If x=w^254 in GF(2^8), then x²w=x and x⁴w=x³, including at w=0. In conjugate coordinates these give x_(m+1) w_m=x_m and x_(m+2) w_m=x_(m+1) x_m for every m modulo8. They are quadratic in the lifted variables, although scalar polynomial degrees differ.
property.quantifier: For every byte w and its canonical inverse x, and each conjugate coordinate m in0..7, at every AES-128 state or key-schedule inversion.
property.scope: Additional necessary quadratic constraints stated in Section6.2. They do not alone characterize inversion, supply a completed zero-inclusive MQ system, or establish an efficient AES key recovery.

parameters.meaning: Rijndael field with polynomial X^8+X^4+X^3+X+1.

parameters.name: identities
parameters.meaning: Original source identities, with m cyclic modulo8.

parameters.name: zero_case
parameters.meaning: Different from the source inverse-product equation xw=1, which excludes zero.

validation.description: All16 original pages read. Independently evaluated both scalar identities for all256 bytes, includingzero;512identity checks passed. The spurious pair x=0,w=1 demonstrates that these equations alone are insufficient. No solver or attack executed.

target.description: Four consecutive normal Rijndael rounds on a 128-bit state. The source combines the 25-active-S-box bound with single-S-box differential weights; this is a predicted trail-product model, not a fixed-key differential-hull bound.

setting.key_relation: One arbitrary fixed sequence of round keys; the two executions of a differential use the same sequence. Round keys need not be identical to one another.
setting.key_population: All fixed round-key sequences for the stated structural property; product-model qualifications are stated separately.
setting.plaintext_model: Nonzero differential or linear trails on the 128-bit Rijndael state.
assumptions: The all-zero trail is excluded.
Standard 128-bit Rijndael S-box, ShiftRows and MixColumns; not related-key differences.

Per-step probability products are the source predicted quantity. No assertion that every fixed-key four-round trail has this exact probability is made; Annex Eq. 5.22 explicitly limits that approximation.

success.description: A mathematical supporting property, not a numerical whole-attack success probability.

property.statement: The AES S-box has maximum differential propagation ratio 2^-6. At least 25 active S-boxes in a nonzero four-round trail therefore give restriction weight at least 150 and a source predicted trail-product quantity at most 2^-150. Section 8.2.3 also gives the eight-round corollary: restriction weight at least 300 and predicted product at most 2^-300.
property.quantifier: Every nonzero four-round activity trail has the stated additive restriction-weight lower bound; the numerical probability is a product-model prediction, not a universal exact probability for each fixed key.
property.scope: Individual trail weights only. A differential sums trails; fixed-key actual propagation counts are integer multiples of 2^-128. The independently supplied Annex explicitly warns that the product approximation fails once the weight reaches the state size.

target.description: Initial AddRoundKey followed by three normal AES rounds, each with MixColumns and AddRoundKey. A 256-state set has one varying input byte and 15 fixed input bytes.

setting.key_relation: One ordinary AES master key and its standard dependent key expansion; no related, known or chosen key is required.
setting.key_population: All AES-128, AES-192 and AES-256 keys.
setting.plaintext_model: A Lambda set of256 plaintexts: one byte takes all256 values and the other15 bytes remain constant.
assumptions: Each S-box is bijective; standard128-bit ShiftRows and MixColumns.

property.statement: Starting from one active input byte, after one normal round one column is active; after two rounds every byte takes all256 values across the Lambda set. This remains true before third-round MixColumns. Linearity of MixColumns and the even cardinality of the set imply that every state byte XORs to0 after three normal rounds. A subsequent S-box layer generally destroys this balance.
property.quantifier: For every AES key, choice of active byte and constants in the other15 plaintext bytes, the XOR of each of the16 output bytes across all256 states is0 at the stated endpoint.
property.scope: Three-round structural supporting property, separated from the four-, five- and six-round secret-key recovery attacks and their data/time budgets.

parameters.meaning: One complete byte value set; not an attack data-complexity claim.

parameters.name: Balanced output
parameters.meaning: Byte-wise integral balance after third-round MixColumns and AddRoundKey.

validation.description: 192 independent 256-state forward sets checked: three key lengths, four deterministic keys/plaintext constants and16 active positions. Every byte is a permutation after round2 and before third MixColumns, and balanced after round3. FIPS197 known-answer vectors verify each key schedule. No key guessing or recovery was run.

observations.reported: U_h defined in line7; line24 return rho_h^(A_min)*Delta_lambda; A_min not assigned in Figure3.

setting.key_relation: One unknown AES-128 key and its standard expanded keys. Key-independent means the algorithm does not know the key; it is neither known-key nor related-key.
setting.key_population: General secret AES-128 keys; no weak-key selection. Numerical theory uses the source binomial/independent-event model; author experiments choose keys with drand48().

assumptions: x and y count pairs/iterations, not individual queries. Nominal D=4xy counts two encryption and two decryption queries per iteration. The pseudocode can stop early.

The source raises per-byte/word rejection probabilities to4y or2y, and assumes independent outer chains. This is a model for adaptive queries to one fixed permutation, not a reproduced theorem of query independence.
Binomial word/byte counts in Lemmas2/5 are retained as the source model; distinct-pair conditioning and finite-population dependence are not silently replaced by a reviewer probability formula.
The source describes AES-128 in Section2.1 and experiments. No separately reported AES-192/256 numerical point or experiment is inferred here.
Source t lies in{1,2,3}; all reported numerical points retained here use t=2. Decimal log2 budgets are rounded estimates of integer loop bounds.

components.description: Table4 source-reported AES-world correct classifications. The printed numerator and100 trials are observations, not a worst-case or fixed-key guarantee; no saved run-level outcomes were obtained.
